hints: Use integration by parts with $u=x$ and $dv=e^{-2x}dx$.
This gives an antiderivative containing $-\tfrac12xe^{-2x}$ and a remaining exponential integral.
Complete that integral, then evaluate at $x=\tfrac12$ and $x=0$.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$ with:
$$u = x \implies \mathrm{d}u = \mathrm{d}x$$
$$\mathrm{d}v = \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,\mathrm{d}x \implies v = \int \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}$$

Substitute these parts into the integration by parts formula:
$$\int x\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}x\mathrm{e}^{-2x} - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\right)\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}x\mathrm{e}^{-2x} + \dfrac{1}{2}\int \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-1}\right) - \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-1} \quad \left(\text{or } \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2\mathrm{e}}\right)$$
